reopen_history.reason: Downstream SQL-on-FHIR consumers join derived tables on getResourceKey() resource keys, which the port computes internally but drops at the outermost SELECT. The attempt adds the paired key column beside each MIMIC identifier column (subject_id->patient_key, hadm_id->encounter_key, stay_id->icu_encounter_key, specimen_id->specimen_key). Additive and shape-only: both comparison paths project manifest columns explicitly, so no compared value can change. The MIMIC integer columns are retained as the oracle join keys.
reopen_history.superseded_justification: Judge accepted COMPLETED_WITH_DIVERGENCE: the sole 1/73,181 output-row divergence is wholly inherited from bg. Six labevents for specimen 44663261 were irreversibly normalized from 2151-03-14 02:02 to 03:02 by mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_observation_labevents.sql:15,121, with the same loss at mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_specimen_lab.sql:18,58; Observation.issued from fhir_observation_labevents.sql:16,122 is storetime and does not preserve charttime. For stay 33143532, the canonical 02:30 upper bound includes the oracle row but excludes the served 03:02 row, reproducing all five conflicts and four calculated NULLs. No FHIR field or opaque resource id can recover the original wall time; expanding the window or subtracting an hour would corrupt genuine rows. The proven upstream DST loss and its second-order aggregate/window effects are exempt from essential-loss blocking. 73,180/73,181 rows identical; 1/73,181 affected; dependency bg is judge-accepted COMPLETED_WITH_DIVERGENCE.

reopen_history.reason: [replay:data_rebuild] The MIMIC-on-FHIR warehouse was rebuilt on 2026-08-24 after two upstream data defects were fixed: FHIR resources are now generated under UTC, so wall-clock timestamps are no longer shifted an hour across the spring-forward boundary, and Patient.birthDate is now derived from the anchor year and age rather than from the first transfer. This port was carried forward byte-identical to re-measure it against the corrected data -- do not re-author it. Expect previously accepted divergences to have shrunk or gone; if an hour-wide shift still appears, treat it as a finding and establish why the correction did not reach that path rather than accepting it as an upstream artifact.
reopen_history.superseded_justification: Accepted wholly inherited upstream DST divergence: mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_observation_labevents.sql:15,121 casts labevents.charttime through TIMESTAMPTZ and writes the normalized value to Observation.effectiveDateTime; bg exposes that value as bg.charttime. Six labevents for specimen 44663261 moved from 2151-03-14 02:02 to 03:02, so stay 33143532's inclusive 02:30 upper bound excludes the served dependency row and changes one output row's aggregates. mimic-fhir/sql/fhir_specimen_lab.sql:9,18,58 repeats the normalized time, while Observation.issued is storetime at fhir_observation_labevents.sql:16,122; the original wall time is unrecoverable by any FHIR query without forbidden resource-ID inference. All nine field incidences are explained with no residual; 73,180/73,181 rows are identical. The contract's DST-defect exemption applies, and the divergence is inherited from judge-accepted bg.
